scenario: A Console API key pasted into a script, chat, or public repository is used to run up spend and read workspace resources such as files and batches.
threat_source: External attacker using a leaked credential
affected_assets: Console workspaces; Files API content; API spend
treatment: Use identity-backed keys with expiry, set organization and workspace spend limits, keep Admin keys to named admins, and rehearse disable then delete.

scenario: A member publishes an artifact or invites an outside address, exposing deal or investor material to people outside the firm.
threat_source: Insider error or social engineering of a member
treatment: Keep external sharing and outside email invitations off, keep public projects off, and review audit exports.

scenario: An unreviewed connector or custom MCP server reads mail and files through a member's token and returns hidden instructions that cause writes.
threat_source: Malicious or compromised MCP server operator
affected_assets: Mailboxes; file stores; CRM records reached through connectors
treatment: Add only reviewed connectors, set write tools to Needs approval or Blocked, restrict verified-domain connectors, and allowlist MCP servers in Claude Code.

scenario: Prompt injection on a web page or document drives Claude in Chrome, code execution, or a Claude Code session to send firm data to an attacker's server.
affected_assets: Browser sessions; code execution sandbox; developer workstations
treatment: Restrict egress, keep Chrome to a pilot with an allowlist, enforce the Claude Code sandbox with managed domains, and isolate computer use.

scenario: A former employee or contractor keeps access to claude.ai or the Console, or a legacy key they created keeps working after they leave.
affected_assets: Chats and projects; Console workspaces; API keys
treatment: Provision through SCIM where available, prove leaver removal, and remove workspace keys that outlive their creator.

scenario: Retention or training settings do not match a client obligation, so chats, project content, or API data are kept longer than promised or used in a way the client forbade.
threat_source: Configuration drift or unreviewed plan change
affected_assets: Client data in chats, projects, and API calls
treatment: Record each obligation, set chat and project retention, confirm ZDR per organization, approve ineligible features, and keep staff off personal accounts.

scenario: Uncontrolled spend from a runaway agent, a leaked key, or usage credits without limits exhausts the budget or pauses production API access at the tier cap.
affected_assets: API budget; production availability; seat usage credits
treatment: Set organization, workspace, and usage-credit limits and review usage weekly.

scenario: Organization instructions, managed Claude Code settings, or a repository CLAUDE.md are changed without review, or conflict, so Claude follows the wrong guidance or a control silently disappears.
threat_source: Insider error or compromised Owner account
affected_assets: Organization instructions; managed settings; repository instruction files
treatment: Keep instructions and policy in reviewed version control, limit editors to named Owners, fail closed on missing policy, and lock permission rules to managed settings.

scenario: A developer runs Claude Code with permissions bypassed on a laptop holding production credentials, and an injected instruction deletes or exfiltrates data.
affected_assets: Developer workstations; production credentials; source code
treatment: Disable bypass mode, decide on auto mode, enforce the sandbox without unsandboxed retry, and allow only managed hooks.

scenario: Audit evidence ages out: the 180-day audit export window passes before an incident is investigated, or the Compliance API was never enabled.
affected_assets: Audit logs; compliance activity feed; investigation capability
treatment: Export audit logs monthly to the evidence store and enable the Compliance API with a least-privilege key.

scenario: Staff use personal Claude accounts or other organizations on firm networks and devices, moving firm data outside the firm's retention and training terms.
treatment: Require SSO, restrict organization creation, inject Tenant Restrictions, and pin Claude Desktop and Claude Code logins to the firm organization.
